name: Jeezy
notes: The sparsest kit in this batch, and every number here is an absence rather than an addition. The research: "very sparse — kick on 1 and the 'and' of 2, clap on 3, hats mostly straight 8ths with occasional 16th doubles; almost no continuous rolls in the 2004–06 records". So `kick.densityPerBar` is [2, 3] with `secondaryAnchor` `2&` and the lowest `syncopation` on this axis; `hihat.continuous` is false with `base` fixed to `8th`, which is what "mostly straight 8ths" means when the rest of the roster is a 16th carpet; and `rolls.freqPerBar` sits at the floor of the band. ⚠ `fillDensity` is 0.32 rather than lower: a model that declares a hat block owes every seed a hat, and below ~0.28 some seeds produce a bar with none. The 808 is "enormous long-decay with slow attack, often the only bass element" with "slides used sparingly as a single up-glide into the downbeat" — hence `slideProb` 0.12, one slide per four bars, and `slidePositions` reduced to the bar line. Harmony is "implied by a drone rather than a progression", so `chords.impliedByRiff` is set and the chord part's variety is carried by `chordDurationBeats` and three `harmonicRhythm` values rather than by families the records do not play. ⚠ `confidence` is `medium` because the research rates this high-medium and says the per-track gear specifics are thin; the INFERRED parameters are every velocity figure, the `2&` kick placement as a probability rather than a fixed grid, and the `i–VI` weight against the static tonic. ⚠ `melody.motifPitchCount` 4 is the research's "low note density (2–4 pitches per bar)" read as a motif size, which is a reading of a density claim rather than a pitch-set claim. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts.
